correctness.rationale: With one client step \(\eta=1/a\) and source scaling \(L=a\), the scaled q-FedAvg client difference equals the exact client gradient. On the scalar quadratic family, each source denominator term equals the exact second derivative of \(F_i^{q+1}/(q+1)\), so the server ratio is exactly \(\Phi_q'/\Phi_q''\). Direct simplification gives the displayed map. On \(|x|<b\), substitution \(q=1/2\) cancels the map identically, while the Taylor coefficient \(2q(2q-1)/(3b^2)\) proves uniqueness among \(q>0\) and exact cubic order otherwise. The \(q=1\) map and contraction bound are exact.

value.rationale: The q parameter is the defining fairness knob of q-FFL, and the source explicitly raises convergence-speed sensitivity to q as a practical concern. The accepted result gives a complete local classification on the simplest heterogeneous-client geometry: all positive exponents except one are exactly cubic, their leading error changes sign at \(q=1/2\), and \(q=1/2\) becomes interval-wide one-round termination. This is a structural solver phenomenon rather than a parameter substitution, and it explains when the source's Hessian-inspired denominator ceases to be merely a bound and becomes an exact Newton curvature.
